passages.text: My son, keep my words and treasure my commandments within you.
passages.sermon:
A father speaks to his son.
He gives his son advice.
He says, “My son, listen to my words.”
He tells his son to keep his words.
He tells his son to treasure his commandments.
He wants his son to keep his commandments within him.
passages.original: בְּ֭נִי שְׁמֹ֣ר אֲמָרָ֑י וּ֝מִצְוֺתַ֗י תִּצְפֹּ֥ן אִתָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: Keep my commandments and live; guard my teachings as the apple of your eye.
passages.sermon:
God gives commandments.
\r\nGod wants you to keep His commandments.
\r\nIf you keep God's commandments, you will live.
\r\nGod gives teachings.
\r\nGuard God's teachings.
\r\nGuard them as carefully as you protect your own eyes.
passages.original: שְׁמֹ֣ר מִצְוֺתַ֣י וֶחְיֵ֑ה וְ֝תוֹרָתִ֗י כְּאִישׁ֥וֹן עֵינֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Tie them to your fingers; write them on the tablet of your heart.
passages.sermon:
A father speaks to his son.
He gives his son advice.
He tells his son to keep his words and commandments.
He says, “Tie my words to your fingers.”
He says, “Write my commandments on the tablet of your heart.”
He wants his son to remember his teachings always.
He wants his son to keep his teachings close at all times.
passages.original: קָשְׁרֵ֥ם עַל־ אֶצְבְּעֹתֶ֑יךָ כָּ֝תְבֵ֗ם עַל־ ל֥וּחַ לִבֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: Say to wisdom, “You are my sister,” and call understanding your kinsman, that they may keep you from the adulteress, from the stranger with seductive words.
passages.sermon:
Wisdom is precious and close.
Treat wisdom as your sister.
Understanding is important and trustworthy.
Call understanding your close relative.
Wisdom and understanding will protect you.
They will keep you safe from the adulteress.
They will guard you from the stranger who uses seductive words.
passages.original: אֱמֹ֣ר לַֽ֭חָכְמָה אֲחֹ֣תִי אָ֑תְּ וּ֝מֹדָ֗ע לַבִּינָ֥ה תִקְרָֽא׃ לִ֭שְׁמָרְךָ מֵאִשָּׁ֣ה זָרָ֑ה מִ֝נָּכְרִיָּ֗ה אֲמָרֶ֥יהָ הֶחֱלִֽיקָה׃

passages.text: For at the window of my house I looked through the lattice.
passages.sermon: I stood in my house.\r\nI looked out the window.\r\nI looked through the lattice.
passages.original: כִּ֭י בְּחַלּ֣וֹן בֵּיתִ֑י בְּעַ֖ד אֶשְׁנַבִּ֣י נִשְׁקָֽפְתִּי׃

passages.text: I saw among the simple, I noticed among the youths, a young man lacking judgment, crossing the street near her corner, strolling down the road to her house, at twilight, as the day was fading into the dark of the night.
passages.sermon:
I looked out and saw some simple people.
I saw some young men.
I noticed one young man who did not have good judgment.
He walked along the street.
He came near the corner where the woman lived.
He walked down the road that led to her house.
He did this at twilight.
The day was ending.
Night was coming.
It was getting dark.
passages.original: וָאֵ֤רֶא בַפְּתָאיִ֗ם אָ֘בִ֤ינָה בַבָּנִ֗ים נַ֣עַר חֲסַר־ לֵֽב׃ עֹבֵ֣ר בַּ֭שּׁוּק אֵ֣צֶל פִּנָּ֑הּ וְדֶ֖רֶךְ בֵּיתָ֣הּ יִצְעָֽד׃ בְּנֶֽשֶׁף־ בְּעֶ֥רֶב י֑וֹם בְּאִישׁ֥וֹן לַ֝֗יְלָה וַאֲפֵלָֽה׃

passages.text: Then a woman came out to meet him, with the attire of a harlot and cunning of heart.
passages.sermon: A woman came out to meet the young man.\r\nShe wore the clothing of a prostitute.\r\nShe had a cunning heart.
passages.original: וְהִנֵּ֣ה אִ֭שָּׁה לִקְרָאת֑וֹ שִׁ֥ית ז֝וֹנָ֗ה וּנְצֻ֥רַת לֵֽב׃

passages.text: She is loud and defiant; her feet do not remain at home.
passages.sermon:
The woman is loud.
She is defiant.
She does not stay at home.
Her feet do not remain in her house.
passages.original: הֹמִיָּ֣ה הִ֣יא וְסֹרָ֑רֶת בְּ֝בֵיתָ֗הּ לֹא־ יִשְׁכְּנ֥וּ רַגְלֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: Now in the street, now in the squares, she lurks at every corner.
passages.sermon:
The woman is loud and defiant.
She does not stay at home.
She goes out into the street.
She walks in the public squares.
She waits and hides at every corner.
passages.original: פַּ֤עַם׀ בַּח֗וּץ פַּ֥עַם בָּרְחֹב֑וֹת וְאֵ֖צֶל כָּל־ פִּנָּ֣ה תֶאֱרֹֽב׃

passages.text: She seizes him and kisses him; she brazenly says to him: “I have made my peace offerings; today I have paid my vows.
passages.sermon:
The woman is loud and defiant.
She does not stay at home.
She seizes the young man.
She kisses him.
She speaks boldly to him.
She says, “I have made my peace offerings.
Today I have paid my vows.”
passages.original: וְהֶחֱזִ֣יקָה בּ֭וֹ וְנָ֣שְׁקָה־ לּ֑וֹ הֵעֵ֥זָה פָ֝נֶ֗יהָ וַתֹּ֣אמַר לֽוֹ׃ זִבְחֵ֣י שְׁלָמִ֣ים עָלָ֑י הַ֝יּ֗וֹם שִׁלַּ֥מְתִּי נְדָרָֽי׃

passages.text: So I came out to meet you; I sought you, and I have found you.
passages.sermon:
A woman waits outside.  
She looks for someone in the streets and public places.  
She comes out to meet a young man.  
She searches for him.  
She finds him.
passages.original: עַל־ כֵּ֭ן יָצָ֣אתִי לִקְרָאתֶ֑ךָ לְשַׁחֵ֥ר פָּ֝נֶ֗יךָ וָאֶמְצָאֶֽךָּ׃

passages.text: I have decked my bed with coverings, with colored linen from Egypt.
passages.sermon:
A woman speaks to a man.
She says she has prepared her bed.
She has covered her bed with fine coverings.
She used colored linen from Egypt.
passages.original: מַ֭רְבַדִּים רָבַ֣דְתִּי עַרְשִׂ֑י חֲ֝טֻב֗וֹת אֵט֥וּן מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, with aloes, and with cinnamon.
passages.sermon:
A woman speaks to a man she is tempting.
She says, “I have perfumed my bed.”
She used myrrh.
She used aloes.
She used cinnamon.
passages.original: נַ֥פְתִּי מִשְׁכָּבִ֑י מֹ֥ר אֲ֝הָלִ֗ים וְקִנָּמֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Come, let us take our fill of love till morning. Let us delight in loving caresses!
passages.sermon:
A woman speaks to a man.
She says, “Come with me.”
She says, “Let us enjoy love together until morning.”
She says, “Let us find pleasure in each other’s embrace.”
passages.original: לְכָ֤ה נִרְוֶ֣ה דֹ֭דִים עַד־ הַבֹּ֑קֶר נִ֝תְעַלְּסָ֗ה בָּאֳהָבִֽים׃

passages.text: For my husband is not at home; he has gone on a long journey.
passages.sermon:
A married woman speaks.
Her husband is not at home.
Her husband has left the house.
He has gone on a long journey.
passages.original: כִּ֤י אֵ֣ין הָאִ֣ישׁ בְּבֵית֑וֹ הָ֝לַ֗ךְ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ מֵרָחֽוֹק׃

passages.text: He took with him a bag of money and will not return till the moon is full.”
passages.sermon:
The woman's husband is not at home.
He took a bag of money with him.
He left on a long journey.
He will not return until the full moon.
He will be gone for many days.
passages.original: צְֽרוֹר־ הַ֭כֶּסֶף לָקַ֣ח בְּיָד֑וֹ לְי֥וֹם הַ֝כֵּ֗סֶא יָבֹ֥א בֵיתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: With her great persuasion she entices him; with her flattering lips she lures him.
passages.sermon:
A woman uses great persuasion.
She entices a man.
She speaks with flattering lips.
She lures him.
passages.original: הִ֭טַּתּוּ בְּרֹ֣ב לִקְחָ֑הּ בְּחֵ֥לֶק שְׂ֝פָתֶ֗יהָ תַּדִּיחֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: He follows her on impulse, like an ox going to the slaughter, like a deer bounding into a trap, until an arrow pierces his liver, like a bird darting into a snare— not knowing it will cost him his life.
passages.sermon:
A man follows a seductive woman.
He acts without thinking.
He is like an ox going to be killed.
He is like a deer running into a trap.
He keeps going until an arrow strikes his liver.
He is like a bird rushing into a snare.
He does not know this will cost him his life.
passages.original: ה֤וֹלֵ֥ךְ אַחֲרֶ֗יהָ פִּ֫תְאֹ֥ם כְּ֭שׁוֹר אֶל־ טָ֣בַח יָב֑וֹא וּ֝כְעֶ֗כֶס אֶל־ מוּסַ֥ר אֱוִֽיל׃ עַ֤ד יְפַלַּ֪ח חֵ֡ץ כְּֽבֵד֗וֹ כְּמַהֵ֣ר צִפּ֣וֹר אֶל־ פָּ֑ח וְלֹֽא־ יָ֝דַ֗ע כִּֽי־ בְנַפְשׁ֥וֹ הֽוּא׃פ

passages.text: Now, my sons, listen to me, and attend to the words of my mouth.
passages.sermon:
I speak to you as a father.
You are my sons.
Listen to me.
Pay attention to what I say.
Hear the words from my mouth.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֣ה בָ֭נִים שִׁמְעוּ־ לִ֑י וְ֝הַקְשִׁ֗יבוּ לְאִמְרֵי־ פִֽי׃

passages.text: Do not let your heart turn aside to her ways; do not stray into her paths.
passages.sermon:
This warning speaks about a seductive and dangerous woman.
She leads people to destruction.
Do not let your heart turn to her ways.
Do not follow her paths.
Stay away from her ways and her paths.
passages.original: אַל־ יֵ֣שְׂטְ אֶל־ דְּרָכֶ֣יהָ לִבֶּ֑ךָ אַל־ תֵּ֝תַע בִּנְתִיבוֹתֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: For she has brought many down to death; her slain are many in number.
passages.sermon:
The woman described here is dangerous.
She has caused many people to fall.
She has led many to death.
All her victims are strong people.
She has killed a great number.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ רַבִּ֣ים חֲלָלִ֣ים הִפִּ֑ילָה וַ֝עֲצֻמִ֗ים כָּל־ הֲרֻגֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: Her house is the road to Sheol, descending to the chambers of death.
passages.sermon:
This woman’s house leads to Sheol.
Sheol is the place of the dead.
Her house is a road that goes down to death.
Her house descends to the chambers of death.
Anyone who enters her house goes toward death.
passages.original: דַּרְכֵ֣י שְׁא֣וֹל בֵּיתָ֑הּ יֹ֝רְד֗וֹת אֶל־ חַדְרֵי־ מָֽוֶת׃פ
